clinician.trajectory_summary: A 34-year-old woman presented with an abdominal lump, pain, and intermittent fever with chills. Initial workup revealed a left lower abdomen mass. CECT of the abdomen showed a heterogeneous enhancing solid cystic lesion with septations in the left ovary. Surgical removal of the ovarian mass was performed. Gross examination of the specimen showed a mass with cystic and solid areas and black pigmentation. Histopathological examination of the ovarian mass revealed dense inflammation, necrosis, and florid fungal septate hyphae with dichotomous branching, leading to the diagnosis of ovarian Aspergillosis. Post-diagnosis, the patient was treated with intravenous voriconazole and liposomal amphotericin B for ten days. A CECT of the thorax was performed to rule out respiratory involvement, which showed no abnormality.
